intro: Newspapers, television, radio and the internet, and how to pass on something you have read or heard.
p.periódico.consejo: It has an accent on the o: «pe-RYO-di-ko». It is masculine: «el periódico».
p.revista.consejo: It usually comes out every week or every month. The v sounds like b.
p.noticias.consejo: «Las noticias» is also the TV news bulletin. A single one is «una noticia».
p.programa.consejo: Although it ends in -a, it is masculine: «el programa».
p.radio.consejo: It is feminine: «la radio». You «escuchas» the radio.
p.serie.consejo: You say «ver una serie», and each part is a «capítulo».
p.canal.consejo: On TV, a canal is a station. Its plural is «canales».
p.telediario.consejo: It is «tele» + «diario»: the day's news on television.
p.tele.consejo: It is the short, familiar form of «televisión»: «ver la tele».
p.buscar.consejo: A thing goes without «a»: «busco información». A person takes «a»: «busco a Ana».
p.compartir.consejo: You share a photo, a piece of news or a meal. It is a regular verb.
p.apagar.consejo: The g is hard: «a-pa-GAR». Its opposite is «encender» or «poner».
p.en serio.consejo: With «¿en serio?» you ask if something is true. It is a very common reaction.
p.página web.consejo: «Web» is pronounced as in English. «Navegar por internet» is going from page to page.
b1.texto:
Useful verbs: **leer** (a newspaper or magazine), **escuchar** (the radio), **ver** (TV or a series), **navegar por** internet and **buscar** information.

To say where you saw something you use **en**: lo he leído **en** el periódico; lo he visto **en** la tele; lo he encontrado **en** internet.

To turn on or off: **poner la tele** or **apagar la tele**. To ask what is on: **¿Qué ponen** esta noche**?**

To pass on news: **dicen que**… **he leído que**… **he oído que**… After **que** comes a normal sentence: dicen que mañana **hay** tormenta.

To react: **¿En serio?** **¿De verdad?** **¡No me digas!**
b2.f1.texto: I don't read the newspaper any more.
b2.f2.texto: I look for everything on the internet.
b2.f3.texto: They say on the radio that tomorrow there is a storm.
b2.f5.texto: I'm going to put the news on.
b2.f7.texto: They are showing a new series.
b2.f8.texto: But there are too many adverts.
b4.texto:
Three structures to talk about the media:

- **en** + medium = where you saw it: **en el periódico**, **en la tele**, **en internet**.
- **dicen que** / **he leído que** + normal sentence: **dicen que hay tormenta**.
- **poner** for TV: **¿Qué ponen?** (what is on) and **pon la tele** (turn it on).

To turn it off: **apaga la tele**, and you soften the request with **por favor**.
b4.e0.texto: I have read it in the newspaper.
b4.e1.texto: They say there is a storm tomorrow.
b5.titulo: A day between screens and waves
b5.f0.texto: The kitchen radio wakes up the house with soft music.
b5.f1.texto: The announcer's clear voice tells the day's news.
b5.f2.texto: Pablo makes coffee next to the misted window.
b5.f3.texto: Outside, a fine rain wets the grey roofs.
b5.f4.texto: The announcer forecasts strong wind for the afternoon.
b5.f5.texto: At night, the TV lights up the living room with blue lights.
b5.f6.texto: Lucía looks for a new series on the phone screen.
b5.f7.texto: An advert in bright colours suddenly jumps onto the screen.
b5.f8.texto: She shares a web page with her brother.
b5.f9.texto: In the end, Lucía switches off the TV and listens to the rain.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Poner» here means to broadcast, to show on TV.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That would be «¿qué te pones?». There is no «te» here.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The time is asked with «¿a qué hora…?».
b6.pregunta: What does «¿qué ponen esta noche?» ask?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «A» shows destination. For the medium you use «en».
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The medium takes «en»: en el periódico, en la tele.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Por» is not normal here. You say «en el periódico».
b7.pregunta: Which word goes with the medium where you read it?
b8.traduccion: They say there is a storm tomorrow
b9.o0.refuerzo: An advert sells something; it does not give news.
b9.o1.refuerzo: A magazine is on paper, not a TV programme.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! It is the TV news bulletin.
b9.pregunta: Which programme gives the news on television?
b10.frase: ____ la tele, por favor. No puedo estudiar.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Well done! Switching the TV off makes it stop sounding.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Pon» switches it on. It would make more noise.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Busca» is trying to find something. It does not switch the TV off.
b10.pregunta: Which command do you need to study without noise?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I read the newspaper».
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Hasta luego» is a goodbye, not a reaction.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes! With «¿en serio?» you ask if it is true.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Buenos días» is a greeting, not a reaction.
b12.pregunta: What do you say if a piece of news surprises you?
p.anuncios.consejo: It comes from «anunciar». The «c» in «anuncio» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.moja.consejo: The «j» sounds like «h». The verb is «mojar», to make wet.
p.anuncia.consejo: The «ci» is «thya» in Spain. The verb is «anunciar».
p.anuncio.consejo: Singular of «anuncios». The «c» before «i» is «th» in Spain.
p.comparte.consejo: From «compartir». The «c» before «o» is «k», and the stress is on «PAR».
p.empañada.consejo: It comes from «paño». The «ñ» sounds like «ny», so say «em-pa-NYA-da».
